messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 PAGING ONCALL — Dedicated EU-WEST pool saturation detected. Multiple customers reporting streaming stalls.
incident-bot: Summary metrics: p95 streaming latency jumped from ~420ms -> ~1.2s, p99 from ~2.4s -> ~6.8s. Queue depth increased x7. Autoscaler applied new slots but warmup handshake lag ~85–120s. Marking P1.

maria: oncall (maria) here — ack. Starting runbook check. Any customer-visible errors?

james: looking at routing and autoscaler logs now. Seeing a flurry of "handshake_timeout" entries when new hotshot nodes try to register.

kai: I can see KV cache cold-path thrashing for some large multi-turn requests, + heavy batch size spikes from a handful of clients. Possibly a handful of power-users creating tail storms.

maria: ok. Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) increase handshake timeout window to 180s while we stabilize, 2) enable extra burst nodes from spare Dedicated pool (if available), 3) route heavy customers to fallback smaller-context model to reduce warmup cost. Which is least risky?

sre-runbook: recommended order per runbook: A) open temporary rate-limit for unknown heavy routes, B) trigger manual capacity add if autoscaler failing, C) fallback routing. Do A immediately.

james: running quick grep on autoscaler logs:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] autoscaler: request_scale delta=+18 target_pool=dedicated-eu-west
[2026-03-15T09:12:45Z] node-provisioner: allocated 18 nodes, provisioning_start=2026-03-15T09:12:46Z
[2026-03-15T09:14:12Z] node-register: handshake_timeout id=node-az2-7d
[2026-03-15T09:14:20Z] node-register: handshake_timeout id=node-az2-8f
[2026-03-15T09:15:10Z] autoscaler: observed_warmup_failures=6
```
james: so autoscaler requested nodes but registration is failing during serving runtime warmup (likely long model load or kernel JIT stalls).

maria: taking action: applying temporary rate limit on routes with highest token rates. @product-ops please prep a short customer-facing note for impacted accounts.

product-ops: drafting now. Do we have a list of top 5 impacted customers? I can coordinate CSMs.

kai: grabbing top offenders via shard telemetry. Early list (anonymized): cust-A (chat multi-turn, 1.5k req/min), cust-B (long-context embedding-heavy), cust-C (streaming voice -> text -> model). I'll DM full IDs to CS.

maria: manual scale request to infra: engaging spare burst capacity in eu-west pool. If burst nodes appear, hold new traffic to them until warmup confirmed. I'll also increase handshake timeout to 180s for registration window (quick config change).

james: changing handshake timeout config now. Command: `redwoodctl config set serving.handshake_timeout 180s --env=eu-west`

james: applied, rolling out across control-plane nodes (non-disruptive).

incident-bot: NOTE: autoscaler issued previously but several nodes failed warmup. Investigating warmup logs for the serving runtime.

kai: found repeated GPU OOMs during model load on a subset of nodes: logs show quantized kernel selection falling back to slower paths and exceeding memory due to concurrent preload. Excerpt:
```
[serve] load_model model=redwood-large-q4_0 path=/mnt/models/rw-large-q4
[serve] gpu_mem_check: available=14.8GB required=18.2GB -> fallback to host staging -> increased swap usage -> warmup timeout
```

kai: looks like the new kernel selection heuristics on that GPU type choose a variant that's too large; we might need to pin a lower-memory kernel or reduce concurrent preload parallelism.

maria: mitigation plan: 1) disable concurrent preloads on new burst nodes (reduce warmup pressure), 2) pin kernel fallback to q4_1 memory-light variant for eu-west temp, 3) keep rate limits in place until KV cache warms. Assigning owners: james -> disable concurrent preloads + handshake change verified, kai -> kernel pin + probe, maria -> customer comms & burst orchestration, product-ops -> CS notifications.

james: disabling concurrent preload on provisioner: `redwoodctl provisioner set preload_concurrency 1 --pool=dedicated-eu-west`

james: done. Observing reduced OOMs on new nodes (prelim).

kai: applying kernel pin override for eu-west for redwood-large-q4_0 -> q4_1. Command run via model-ops. Monitoring.

incident-bot: Telemetry update (09:28Z): queue depth down from x7 -> x2. p95 latency trending down to ~560ms. p99 still elevated ~3.2s with occasional streaming stalls.

maria: good. Now need to triage customer impact severity and determine if we need to page any enterprise customers directly. product-ops, CS, what's threshold for outbound?

product-ops: target threshold is >20% request errors or >30% sustained p99 increase that affects SLAs. We're at intermittent stalls and retries for a small set of customers. Recommend targeted outreach rather than broad incident notification. Drafting templates.

maria: agreed — targeted outreach. CS, send to top-affected list with mitigation steps and ETA for full recovery. We'll keep status updates every 15m in thread.

james: warmup success rate improved after preload change. New nodes registering now. Handshake events: successful registrations at 09:31Z+.

incident-bot: Telemetry update (09:38Z): p95 ~480ms, p99 ~1.1s, streaming stalls rare. Autoscaler backlog resolved; observed_warmup_failures dropped to 1.

kai: still seeing a small class of very long-context requests (>=32k tokens) that are causing cold KV hits and long stall spikes. We should consider short-term guardrails: queue-weight isolation or route them to a dedicated coldpath pool.

maria: can we do a soft-fail for ultra-long contexts? i.e., reject with 429 + hint to retry with smaller window? That avoids degrading majority.
kai: yes, we can apply a policy rule on edge router: if context_len > 20k then return 429 + link to docs. I'll push a config.

james: deploying context_len guard now. `redwoodctl routing add-rule --match 'context_len>20000' --action rate_limit/429 --pool=dedicated-coldpath`

james: applied. Expect to reduce KV coldpath storms.

incident-bot: Telemetry update (09:52Z): p95 430ms, p99 620ms. Queue depth normalized. Streaming stalls resolved for >95% traffic.

maria: excellent. We're moving to recovery mode. Remaining actions: - Follow up with model-ops to make kernel-selection heuristic more conservative on this GPU family (kai) - Post-incident runbook update: autoscaler should detect warmup failure pattern and retry with different kernel/preset instead of burning attempts (sre-runbook) - CS outreach completed (product-ops).

product-ops: CS outreach sent to top 5 customers at 09:55Z. Template includes explanation, mitigation, and ETA for postmortem.

sre-runbook: adding a postmortem owner and runbook task: owner=kai, secondary=james. Include action to add warmup-failure alarm that triggers automated kernel fallback after 3 consecutive handshakes fail.

maria: taking incident to RCA. Will close this paging thread once the postmortem doc is created. Thanks team. Closing note: root cause = combination of burst hotshot traffic causing many concurrent model preloads + GPU kernel memory heuristic selecting high-memory kernel -> warmup OOMs -> autoscaler retries failed -> queue buildup -> customer-visible p99 spikes.

oncall-bot: Incident P1 -> transitioned to P0? (auto-comment). Please file postmortem with timeline and customer impact tags.

maria: filing postmortem now and assigning to kai. Will link doc here when ready.

james: leaving final note: consider keeping preload_concurrency at 1 for this model family until model-ops delivers kernel heuristic fix.

maria: thread will be closed once postmortem link posted. Great work everyone. :thumbsup:
